expl: The historical period is determined on the basis of the knowledge of a decipherable script. The period before the knowledge of writing is called the prehistoric period. In Indian history, the period from about 3000 BC to 600 BC is considered protohistoric. The Indus Civilization belongs to the protohistoric period because writing was known here, but it has not been deciphered so far.

stem: What is the most significant feature of the Indus Valley Civilization?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The main feature of the Indus Valley Civilization is considered to be town planning. Here, cities and towns were established according to a fixed plan. Among the buildings made of burnt bricks, the Great Bath and the Granary of Mohenjodaro. Their surfaces were made of burnt bricks and were joined with gypsum. Buildings made of burnt bricks, planned architecture, and advanced trade and commerce were the major characteristics of this civilization. It is noteworthy that, unlike ancient civilizations such as Mesopotamia and Egypt, clear evidence of places of worship is not found in the Harappan Civilization. Similarly, the first true arch in India is seen in Balban’s tomb. Therefore, option (e) is the correct answer.

stem: Which city is known as 'Mini Harappa'?
expl: Lothal was one of the southernmost cities of the ancient Harappan/Indus Civilization. It is also known as “Mini Harappa”. It is located in the present-day state of Gujarat. Its initial excavation was carried out under the direction of Prof. S. R. Rao.

stem: Which of the following is a Harappan port?
expl: The Harappan town of Lothal is located on the bank of the Bhogava River in Ahmedabad district of Gujarat. It was a Harappan-period port, from where evidence of a dockyard has been found.

stem: Which of the following is a Harappan site in Gujarat?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/ More than one of the above

expl: Lothal is in Gujarat, Kalibangan is in Rajasthan, Dabarkot is in Balochistan (Pakistan), and Rakhigarhi is in Haryana.

stem: Which is the oldest civilization in the world?
expl: The Mesopotamian Civilization (Iraq) is considered the oldest civilization in the world. This civilization developed in present-day Iraq and the surrounding regions. The Egyptian Civilization developed in the Nile Valley and is considered to be later than the Mesopotamian Civilization.

stem: Which of the following animals was not known to the people of the Indus Valley Civilization?
expl: Among the given options, the people of the Indus Valley Civilization were familiar with the bull and the elephant, but scholars differ regarding the presence of the horse. It is difficult to determine with certainty whether the bones obtained from various Harappan sites belong to the wild ass/ onager (Equus hemionus khur) or to the domesticated horse (Equus caballus). Evidence of the horse, or other animals of the same group, has been reported from Rangpur, Rana Ghundai, Lothal, Surkotada, Kuntasi and Kalibangan. A scholar reported that among the so-called horse remains found from Surkotada, six were genuine horse remains dating to around 2000 BCE, i.e., around the middle of the last part of the third millennium BCE. In 1974, J.P. Joshi and A.K. Sharma of the Archaeological Survey of India reported that horse bones were found at every level here between 2100– 1700 BCE. However, Ramsharan Sharma, Romila Thapar, Mando, etc., do not accept this. Similarly, the teeth claimed to be of a horse by Brigadier E.J. Ross from the Early Harappan site of Rana Ghundai are considered inauthentic by Zauner. Therefore, regarding the horse, it would be appropriate to say that its presence in the Harappan Civilization cannot be completely denied, though its use must have been extremely limited. The Bihar Public Service Commission accepted option (b) as the answer.

stem: Which among the following Harappan sites was terracotta of a 'plough' was found?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Among the given options, terracotta replicas connected with a plough have been found from the Indus Valley sites of Banawali (Haryana) and Kalibangan (Rajasthan). According to the Archaeological Survey of India, at Kalibangan, along with a ploughed field from the early phase, a terracotta plough (replica/model) was also found. In addition, a terracotta plough (replica/model) has also been found from the ancient site of Banawali located in Fatehabad district of Haryana.

stem: In which of the following Harappan cities, furrows of ploughed fields have been found?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: A terracotta replica/model of a plough has been found from Banawali located in Fatehabad district of Haryana. Evidence of a dockyard has been found from Lothal, situated near the Gulf of Khambhat (on the bank of the Bhogava River). Evidence of ploughed fields has been found from Kalibangan located on the bank of the Ghaggar River in Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan. From Dholavira (Gujarat), a wooden signboard containing 10 large-sized signs of the Harappan script has been found.

stem: Who among the following was not associated with the excavation of Harappa and Mohenjodaro?
expl: In 1921, Dayaram Sahni started large-scale excavation work at Harappa. From 1926–27 to 1933–34, Madho Sarup Vats remained associated with the excavation work at Harappa. Mohenjodaro was first discovered in 1922 by Rakhaldas Banerjee, who drew attention to its archaeological importance. Besides them, some other scholars—K.N. Dikshit, Ernest Mackay, Aurel Stein, A.N. Ghosh, J.P. Joshi, etc.—also made important contributions to the study of this civilization. Thus, it is clear that V.A. Smith was not associated with the excavation work related to the Harappan Civilization; rather, he was famous as an Indologist and historian.

stem: Which colour was commonly used in the Harappan Pottery?
expl: The people of Harappa produced earthen pots on a large scale, and traces of red colour are found on them. In the Harappan civilization, the potter’s wheel was also used to make pottery. On the basis of design, these pots were of two categories— plain (without design) pots and painted pottery. Sand was mixed with the clay used for making pottery; after firing, it took on a light brownish-red colour. The upper portion of these pots was coated with red paint, and the lower portion was decorated with various designs in black colour.

stem: According to the report of the IIT Kharagpur study group, continuous low rainfall for how many years was the cause of the fall of the Indus Valley Civilization?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to a report released in 2018 by a study team of the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, the Indus Valley Civilization declined due to a drought that continued for 900 years. It is noteworthy that scholars like Aurel Stein also considered climatic change to be a major reason for the decline of the Harappan civilization.
